topic: Typhoon development, structure, and land/water effects
key_concepts: A typhoon is a mature tropical cyclone in the western North Pacific Ocean
Equivalent storms are called hurricanes in the Atlantic and northeastern Pacific
In the Philippines, all tropical cyclone categories are called bagyo
A tropical cyclone has rain bands, an eye, and an eyewall
Air pressure is lowest at the eye, so surrounding air blows toward it
Wind speed is greatest at the eyewall and calm at the eye
Typhoons form over warm ocean water when rising moist air condenses and releases heat
PAGASA classifies tropical cyclones into five categories by wind speed
Landmasses weaken typhoons by blocking warm water and water vapor supply
Warm bodies of water supply the moisture and energy that sustain typhoons
A storm surge is an abnormal rise of seawater during a typhoon
PAGASA raises typhoon signals based on wind strength and speed
